description: Write a PySpark ETL script for health_portal that tokenizes the national identifier in two tables (patients and claims) so that the tables remain joinable after tokenization. The script should: (1) normalize national_id to digits only, (2) compute patient_token as the first 16 hex characters of HMAC-SHA256(key, normalized id), with the key loaded from a secret scope (the sample uses the key 'corpus_test_key'), (3) apply the identical function to both tables, (4) drop national_id from both outputs, (5) verify that the number of claims matching a patient is the same before and after tokenization and that no two distinct identifiers share a token. All identifiers in the sample are synthetic. Rows are tagged with _dataset = patients or claims.
edge_cases: The same identifier is formatted differently in the two tables (dashes, spaces, leading whitespace); without normalization the tokens differ and all three claims become orphans
A random token or per-run salt (uuid, monotonically_increasing_id) is not reproducible across tables or runs
An unkeyed hash of a 9-digit identifier can be reversed by enumerating all values; a keyed HMAC is required
Join cardinality must be asserted before and after: 3 matched claims in both cases
Truncating to 16 hex characters requires a collision check
common_failure_modes: FM1: Inconsistent normalization between tables silently breaks the post-tokenization join
FM7: No before/after join reconciliation, so the lost matches go unnoticed
FM7: national_id column retained in one of the outputs
